fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the target as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with an unspecified single-phase alloy.
The proposed oxygen-complex intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of controlled aging across the 550–750°C ordering and phase-boundary-evolution window.
The mechanism omits L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, dislocation pile-ups, and crack initiation at phase-boundary tips.
It predicts generic toughness preservation rather than the observed non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition with minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The cited evidence supports oxygen-related strengthening or strength–ductility improvement, but not preservation of toughness after thermal exposure or stability of ordered oxygen complexes at 700°C.
explanation: The proposal is testable and includes an appropriate intervention-free control, but it does not reconstruct the material, treatment, mediator, mechanism, or temperature-dependent outcome of the target. Its 700°C exposure falls broadly within the relevant thermal interval, yet no exposure duration, loading protocol, oxygen concentration, or regime boundaries are defined. The falsification experiment could determine whether oxygen improves bulk mechanical performance, but it would not distinguish the proposed solid-solution/load-transfer mechanism or the target phase-boundary mechanism because it lacks structural measurements such as TEM/TKD of ordering, dislocation pile-ups, and crack-initiation sites. The evidence only establishes that ordered oxygen complexes can enhance strength and ductility in some HEAs; it does not validate post-aging toughness retention, so the central extrapolation remains unsupported.
